Strongest direct match: [UFRec (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28493) addresses sparse sequential recommendation with confidence-weighted multi-step future supervision plus future-aware contrastive learning. Both auxiliary modules operate only during training, adding no inference overhead. Its central caution: uniformly weighting future supervision can hurt uncertain examples. [EchoRec (2026, under review)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14011) likewise finds future interactions informative but increasingly unreliable across longer horizons as intent changes; it uses ordered auxiliary branches discarded at inference. These support testing future supervision, but do not establish gains for this GRU4Rec benchmark.

Earlier evidence is adjacent: [HeterRec (SIGIR 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01469) introduces Listwise Multi-step Prediction within a heterogeneous-feature Transformer. [STAMP (2026, under review)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05329) densifies supervision through auxiliary multi-token prediction, but semantic-ID tokens differ from future interaction items. [SSDRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04278) highlights noise and unreliable modeling in short histories, reinforcing the need to avoid assuming every distant interaction reflects persistent intent.

Practical inference for the constrained experiment: retain one GRU4Rec network per category; jointly train lightweight horizon-specific projections from causal GRU states toward observed training items at offsets +2/+3, alongside the primary next-item loss. Mask padding and unavailable future targets, normalize by valid targets, and test small auxiliary weights with horizon decay or detached confidence weighting. Use only the primary next-item scorer at inference. Compare against the corrected baseline under matched GPU compute and select solely by the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; literature results are motivation, not predicted benchmark gains.
